body:
# Independent audit: strict maximal occupied-face witness count


`candidate 377015272f07c571`.

with the explicitly conditional critical-menu interface in the source.

The midpoint face is exactly the join of the endpoint minimal faces:
any face containing a strict convex combination contains both endpoints,
and any face containing the endpoints contains their midpoint. Hence
same-parity witnesses on two distinct maximal occupied faces would
produce an occupied face strictly containing both, which is impossible.
The parity sets in their relative interiors are therefore disjoint,
and s<=k follows without a full affine-dimensionality assumption.

The matching-parity fact is valid even before saturation. If q has
the parity of witness p_i, their integer midpoint belongs to I, and
its occupied minimal face contains F_i. Maximality forces the face
join to equal F_i, placing q in F_i. No inference of this kind is
made between different parities.

At saturation s=k, all occupied parity labels are witness labels.
If r in relint F_i had another label j, the matching-parity fact
would put r in F_j, whence its minimal face F_i is contained in
F_j, contradicting distinct maximality. Thus every relative-interior
integer point of F_i has label i. For any q with that label, the
midpoint with p_i lies in relint F_i and therefore has the same
label again. Iterating produces p_i+2^(-h)(q-p_i) in the finite I
for every h. If q differs from p_i these points are distinct, so
finiteness forces each parity class to be a singleton witness.

Now any vertex of F_i is a vertex of conv(I), hence is an element
of I and therefore another witness p_j. Its minimal face is the
singleton vertex, and maximality of that F_j forces F_i to equal
it. Thus all occupied faces are singleton vertices, proving the
exact forward equality classification. The converse is immediate.
The argument includes k=1, n=0, and lower-dimensional affine hulls.

The strict bound s<=k-1 follows for every nonexceptional configuration,
not only when |I|>k. The source's sharp example has integer points
exactly 0,e_1,2e_1,e_2,...,e_(k-1): its displayed simplex inequality
excludes all others. Its k occupied parities and k+1 points have
one occupied edge and k-2 occupied singleton faces, giving s=k-1.
This establishes sharpness in k without implying any extra lattice
width or disjointness property of the maximal faces.

The critical-cover consequence correctly reuses the FIXED witness
selection before circuit choice. The selected circuit covers the
whole plane over its face, while original nondeep and emerging-base
slack groups remain in the full deformed cover. Under the additional
signed linear-response hypotheses, substituting s<=k-1 into the
already proved essential-block rank theorem gives rank<=k-2 with
the same universal-over-circuit-selection and existential-multiplier
quantifiers. For k=2 the single witness has only zero relevant
linear responses. This does not assert all actual nonsmooth cap
responses are linear, or convert vanishing derivatives into a
global depth estimate.

No correction was needed. The proof is finite and analytic and
requires no computational premise.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
